etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: A back-formation from lamentation or else from Middle French lamenter and its etymon Latin lāmentor (“to wail, weep”), from lāmentum (“wailing, moaning, weeping”); with formative -mentum, from the root *la-, probably ultimately imitative. Also see latrare.
senses: An expression of grief, suffering, sadness or regret.
(intransitive) To express grief; to weep or wail; to mourn.
(transitive) To express great sorrow or regret over; to bewail.
